shared_components.rationale: lineitem (60M rows, ~4.8GB columnar) is the largest table and is sequentially scanned by 16 of 22 queries. On HDD (~150MB/s), each independent scan costs ~5s. A single shared scan eliminates 15 redundant reads, saving ~75s of HDD I/O. Each consumer applies its own residual predicates (date ranges, returnflag, shipmode, etc.) at negligible CPU cost during the streaming scan. Even queries with narrow date filters (Q14 at 1.3%, Q15 at 3.9%) that could use zone maps benefit from the free ride since the shared scan is already happening for other consumers.
shared_components.notes: Sorted by l_orderkey, enabling merge join with orders. Consumers Q4 excluded (uses EXISTS via dense_range index, not a sequential scan). Each consumer reads only the column subset it needs from the shared columnar stream.

shared_components.rationale: orders (15M rows, ~750MB) is touched by 11 queries via sequential scan or merge join with lineitem. Both tables are sorted by orderkey, enabling a single-pass merge join for the 8 queries that join lineitem⋈orders. Q4, Q5, Q10 scan orders with date range filters (3.9%-15.7% selectivity); Q13 requires a full scan for LEFT OUTER JOIN. A single shared scan eliminates 10 redundant reads, saving ~12s of HDD I/O. Queries with date filters (Q4, Q5, Q10) apply residual predicates during the stream.
shared_components.notes: Sorted by o_orderkey, co-sorted with lineitem for merge join. Q22 excluded (uses custkey_to_orders grouped_fk index for NOT EXISTS check). Q13 needs o_comment for NOT LIKE filter.

shared_components.rationale: partsupp (8M rows, ~320MB) is scanned by 5 queries. Q2 joins partsupp with part+supplier for minimum cost supplier lookup. Q9 joins partsupp with lineitem for profit calculation. Q11 aggregates partsupp with supplier (filtered by nation). Q16 joins partsupp with part for supplier count. Q20 uses partsupp in a semi-join subquery. Sharing eliminates 4 redundant scans, saving ~2s. Existing indexes (partsupp_partkey_idx, composite_hash, suppkey_grouped) handle point lookups but not full scans.
shared_components.notes: Sorted by (ps_partkey, ps_suppkey). ps_comment column excluded from output schema as no consumer needs it for computation, saving ~150MB of I/O.

shared_components.rationale: part (2M rows, ~100MB) is scanned with different filter predicates by 4 queries: Q2 (p_size=15, p_type LIKE '%%BRASS'), Q9 (p_name LIKE '%%green%%'), Q16 (p_brand<>'Brand#45', p_type NOT LIKE, p_size IN), Q20 (p_name LIKE 'forest%%'). Each applies different residual filters. Sharing eliminates 3 redundant scans, saving ~600ms. Queries Q8, Q14, Q17, Q19 probe part via dense_pk index from lineitem and do not need the shared scan.
shared_components.notes: p_retailprice and p_comment excluded from output. Queries that join lineitem→part (Q8, Q9, Q14, Q17, Q19) use the dense_pk index for point lookups during the shared lineitem scan and are not listed as consumers here.

rejected_candidates.reason: Both tables are sorted by orderkey enabling a trivial single-pass merge join per consumer. Materializing 60M joined rows would consume ~6GB of memory with no I/O benefit beyond the shared scans already provided. Each consumer can stream the merge join independently.

Customer has a dense_pk index (c_custkey -> row_id) providing O(1) array lookup. Hash build would be redundant. 7 queries probe customer via this index; the 1.5M-row table (120MB) fits in page cache after first access.
Supplier has a dense_pk index (s_suppkey -> row_id). Only 100K rows (8MB). Hash build cost ~3ms; even with 10 consumers, savings of ~27ms do not justify the coordination overhead.
Part has a dense_pk index (p_partkey -> row_id). 2M rows fit in page cache (~100MB). Dense array lookup is faster than hash probing.
Pre-joining supplier (100K) with nation (25 rows) costs ~3ms per build. With 8 consumers the total savings are ~21ms. Below the profitability threshold given coordination overhead.

Q6 and Q20 both filter lineitem by the same l_shipdate range [1994-01-01, 1995-01-01). However, both are already consumers of scan_lineitem_full. Materializing a separate filtered subset (~9.4M rows) would add memory overhead without reducing I/O beyond the shared full scan.
Only Q13 (LEFT JOIN) and Q22 (filtered scan) do sequential customer scans — 2 consumers. Customer is 1.5M rows (120MB), fitting in page cache. Savings of ~100ms do not justify a shared component.
Supplier is only 100K rows (8MB). Scan cost ~50ms. Even with 4 scanning consumers, savings of ~150ms are below the profitability threshold.
Only Q18 needs this aggregation (for HAVING SUM(l_quantity) > 300 subquery). Single consumer — not sharable.

7 queries use this join but with different filters on both sides. Materializing 15M unfiltered rows wastes memory. Customer dense_pk provides O(1) lookup from orders; custkey_to_orders grouped_fk index provides reverse lookup.
